subject: some questions about rApache and brew

messages.author: 56f89e4e966f65cf
messages.subject: some questions about rApache and brew
parts:
Hi,
I have some question when trying to use rApache and brew:

1) I put a brew file in a folder, but I cannot run it, until I restart
apache. Does it mean that if we want to add a new .brew file, we then
must restart apache to use it?

2) I build a page containing 3 links, each of which connect to a brew
file. Then when I click on any of them, the result is random... I can
never know what will I see.
Does it mean that we should only put a single file in a folder?

Thanks for help!

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: some questions about rApache and brew
parts:
On Thu, Feb 23, 2012 at 10:03 PM, Zhenjiang Lan <lan.zh...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
> I have some question when trying to use rApache and brew:
>
> 1) I put a brew file in a folder, but I cannot run it, until I restart
> apache. Does it mean that if we want to add a new .brew file, we then
> must restart apache to use it?

No, that should not be the case. What version of rApache are you running?

Jeff

>
> 2) I build a page containing 3 links, each of which connect to a brew
> file. Then when I click on any of them, the result is random... I can
> never know what will I see.
> Does it mean that we should only put a single file in a folder?

There is a bug in rapache 1.1.16, if you're using that version. The
next release should fix the randomness.

Jeff

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: some questions about rApache and brew
parts:
About the 1st one, which browser you're using for development? I know that Firefox tends to keep stuff in cache, so it's a good practice to reload the page by bypassing the cache (Shift + click on reload button, or Ctrl + Shift + R). And dunno which OS are you using, but oftentimes you can just reload configuration, without restarting, e.g, I use Arch Linux, and I can do: rc.d reload httpd. But still, that shouldn't happen.

aL3xa
